conditions.name: OCD
conditions.note: A 2023 systematic review (Law et al.) and a dysbiosis-centred review (Bendriss et al.) corroborate this profile: OCD shows LOWER gut α-diversity (species richness/evenness) and the recurring pattern of increased Alistipes (Rikenellaceae) alongside depletion of Prevotellaceae and butyrate producers (Oscillospira, Odoribacter, Anaerostipes, Agathobacter, Coprococcus, Lachnospira) — with Lachnospira pectinoschiza depletion tracking obsession-subscale severity. Direction isn't settled: a saliva/blood study found Actinobacteria and Firmicutes raised, and a natural-OCD deer-mouse model showed increased Desulfovermiculus, Aestuariispira, Peptococcus, Holdemanella and families Lachnospiraceae/Ruminococcaceae (animal — and opposite to the human Lachnospiraceae depletion). Probiotic signal: Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG and L. casei attenuate OCD-like behaviour in rodents; no human RCT yet.

conditions.note: EVIDENCE BASE IS THIN. As of 2026, exactly one primary 16S study exists (Rössler 2022, n = 24 unmedicated BPD women vs 21 HC women — all-female cohort). conditions.name: Parkinson's disease
conditions.note: The most robust, best-replicated gut-microbiome signal in neurology. The recurring pattern: mucin-layer-degrading Akkermansia up, SCFA/butyrate producers (Roseburia, Faecalibacterium, Lachnospiraceae, Blautia, Fusicatenibacter) down. Nishiwaki showed this holds across countries and is independent of constipation, BMI, sex, age and COMT-inhibitor use. Mechanistic throughline: butyrate loss + mucus-layer degradation → barrier permeability → enteric α-synuclein. Caveats: directions are for established PD; COMT inhibitors independently raise Lactobacillaceae, and disease stage shifts the picture (Faecalibacterium/Fusicatenibacter depletion predicts faster progression).

conditions.note: Well-controlled case-control (Minerbi 2019): 77 women with FM vs matched controls, with differences independent of diet, physical activity, medication and comorbid IBS, and taxa abundance tracking symptom severity. conditions.name: Anorexia nervosa
conditions.note: IMPORTANT — most of these shifts are downstream of the semi-starved, low-BMI state itself, not a cause. Methanobrevibacter smithii tracks inversely with BMI, faecal SCFA excretion falls on a hypocaloric diet, and several changes partially (though often incompletely) renormalise with weight restoration. The one causal signal is Fan 2023, where transplanting AN microbiota into germ-free mice transferred an anorexia-like phenotype — so the microbiome may also feed back onto the illness. Functionally, gut-brain modules for serotonin biosynthesis and for dopamine / glutamate / tryptophan degradation are enriched in AN, a plausible route to mood and appetite effects. Evidence is heterogeneous (small cohorts, few at species level, starvation a massive confound) — read the taxa as an illness-state signature, not a target.

conditions.note: EVIDENCE IS THIN AND INCONSISTENT — small, paediatric tic-disorder (TD/TS) cohorts, mostly single-centre, with no consensus on α- or β-diversity and taxa that move in opposite directions across studies; treat directions as tentative. The most reproducible signals are increased Bacteroides and Ruminococcus (Ruminococcus lactaris especially enriched in TS specifically) and decreased Bifidobacterium. A GABA thread runs through the data and may interest you: the GABA-degrading Klebsiella pneumoniae rises with symptom deterioration, while GABA-producing Bifidobacterium, Eubacterium and Akkermansia muciniphila are inversely correlated with tic severity (YGTSS) — yet, oppositely, some GABA-producing Bacteroides species (B. thetaiotaomicron, B. eggerthii, B. dorei) correlate positively with severity. Notable conflicts: one drug-naive-TD cohort (Wang 2022) found Prevotella and Faecalibacterium INCREASED, opposite to the depletion seen in most other conditions here, and Odoribacter is up in TD but down in OCD. A probiotic/FMT signal exists (Limosilactobacillus reuteri; small FMT case series) but no definitive RCT.

conditions.name: Multiple sclerosis
conditions.note: Autoimmune demyelinating CNS disease. The flagship iMSMS shotgun study (576 patients + genetically unrelated household controls) is the strongest dataset: it reports enrichment of Akkermansia muciniphila, Ruthenibacterium lactatiformans, Hungatella hathewayi and Eisenbergiella tayi, and depletion of Faecalibacterium prausnitzii and Blautia. The recurring theme is loss of butyrate producers (Faecalibacterium, Roseburia, Coprococcus, Butyricimonas) plus a mucin-degrader (Akkermansia) and methanogen (Methanobrevibacter) rise. Composition also shifts with disease-modifying therapy, so treatment status is a major confound.

conditions.name: Ehlers-Danlos (hypermobile)
conditions.note: Heritable connective-tissue disorder (defects in collagen / ECM). Gut involvement is real and common — chronic GI symptoms in ~80% — but it is a story of dysmotility, small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO) and overlap with IBS/POTS/MCAS, NOT a characterised fecal taxon signature. There is currently no validated microbial biomarker for hEDS, so the entries here are deliberately sparse and flagged as indirect. Included because Kelsey's rheumatologist context makes the EDS/hypermobility axis relevant and because it cross-links strongly to IBS and fibromyalgia.

taxa.name: Small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO)
taxa.note: Not a single taxon — overall small-bowel bacterial load. In hypermobility disorders (including hEDS) with GI symptoms, ~70% meet SIBO criteria on aspirate (≥10^3 CFU/mL); 100% of those with gastroparesis or dyssynergic defecation. Mechanism is connective-tissue-driven dysmotility allowing luminal microbes to proliferate, not a distinctive dysbiotic community.

conditions.name: Endometriosis
conditions.note: Estrogen-dependent inflammatory disease (endometrial-like tissue outside the uterus); frequently comorbid with IBS. Two microbiomes matter — gut and reproductive tract — and the 'estrobolome' (gut microbes that deconjugate estrogens via β-glucuronidase) is the proposed mechanistic link. Gut findings (this atlas' focus): a higher Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes ratio, phylum-level rises in Actinobacteria/Proteobacteria/Verrucomicrobia, loss of Lactobacilli and butyrate producers (Ruminococcaceae, Lachnospira), and severity-dependent shifts (Dialister ↓, Streptococcus/Lactobacillus ↑ with stage; Prevotella/Bacteroides ↓ in advanced disease). Directions are frequently contested between Shan 2020, Svensson 2021 and the 2025 meta-analysis, so several taxa here carry explicit caveats.
